transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood Solutions), Marta Ruiz (OrionCloud PM), Ken Ito (OrionCloud SRE), Liam O'Connor (OrionCloud Marketplace Eng), Aisha Kamal (OrionCloud Security)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time right before the holidays, appreciate it. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: Marta here.
[00:10] Ken Ito: Ken.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Liam.
[00:14] Aisha Kamal: Aisha here.
[00:16] Priya Singh: Priya. Carlos on?
[00:18] Carlos Vega: Yup, Carlos.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Great. Agenda 	6 kickoff on marketplace listing, walk through reference arch for OrionCloud marketplace (VPC/private listing), KMS/HSM and data residency questions, then a short perf/benchmarks plan.

[00:32] Jordan Lee: Marta, can you confirm the goal? My understanding is you want Redwood listed in OrionCloud marketplace as a private partner integration and a reference architecture that customers can deploy in their Orion VPC 	6 is that right?
[00:42] Marta Ruiz: Yes that's right. We want two entry points 	6 a managed listing where our customers can subscribe to Redwood's hosted offering directly from the Orion console, and a "bring-your-own" option where enterprise customers can deploy Redwood Private into their Orion VPC via our marketplace stack.
[00:56] Jordan Lee: Makes sense. We'll need to map how our Private deployment artifacts (Helm charts and the private control plane) line up with your marketplace packaging. Priya's going to take us through the architecture we recommend.

[01:12] Priya Singh: Cool. Quick caveat 	6 some of the names across teams get swapped in transcripts so, um, I'll say Redwood Private (private control plane) and Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) but in the listing we can name them per your naming rules.
[01:25] Priya Singh: OK, architecture slide one 	6 high level: for the private marketplace listing we propose a two-template approach: 1) a managed listing that integrates with OrionCloud SSO and billing APIs, where customer seats are provisioned on Redwood-hosted Dedicated pools; 2) a marketplace AMI/helm bundle that automates deployment of Redwood Private into customer VPC with optional KMS integration.

[01:48] Ken Ito: On the managed option, how do you handle tenant isolation? If a customer subscribes through Orion, are we redirecting tokens to Redwood hosted endpoints or is there a proxying layer?
[01:58] Priya Singh: For managed we issue customer-specific API keys scoped to their org. Requests go to Redwood hosted runtime. We can support per-tenant isolation via dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated) or strict RBAC and org-scoped namespaces. There's also routing rules so high-compute requests can be routed to different regions.

[02:18] Marta Ruiz: For marketplace compliance we need to show audit logs and SOC2 artifacts. Aisha, any initial security blocker?
[02:25] Aisha Kamal: We'll need to validate KMS integration for customer-managed keys and confirm HSM support for certain regulated customers. Also need details on logging 	6 retention windows, export formats, and whether you offer SIEM connectors.

[02:38] Carlos Vega: We have a KMS/HSM integration doc 	6 link: https://redwood.example/docs/kms-integration (note: internal link). For SIEM, we can ship logs to S3 or push to customer's syslog/OTel collectors; we also have per-route audit logging and token-level traces. We should capture Aisha's retention requirements.

[03:00] Aisha Kamal: Typical minimum is 12 months retention for logs for our regulated customers, with export to the customer's S3 in their account. Also need encryption-at-rest certified via KMS.

[03:12] Priya Singh: That aligns with our Private offering where the customer owns the KMS key. For the managed listing, we offer options: Redwood-managed KMS or customer BYOK (bring your own key). BYOK adds a few configuration steps but is supported.

[03:28] Liam O'Connor: On the marketplace artifact 	6 we saw NovaEdge's listing used a CloudFormation/helm combo to pre-wire VPC peering and route tables. Do you require VPC peering or can you do inbound private connectivity?
[03:40] Priya Singh: We support both. If customers want PrivateLink/PrivateServiceConnect style connectivity, we can support a private endpoint. For some Orion network topologies, VPC peering is simpler. The helm chart includes a network preflight that will validate routes.

[03:56] Ken Ito: Network egress 	6 if customers deploy Redwood Private in their VPC, will telemetry phone-home to Redwood control plane? We need explicit opt-in for telemetry.
[04:05] Carlos Vega: Telemetry for managed features is optional 	6 we default to local-only logs unless the customer opts in. For private deployments there's a control-plane connection (for updates and license checks) but that's configurable to be offline for air-gapped installs.

[04:18] Jordan Lee: Switching to listing copy 	6 Marta, what fields do you need from us to populate the marketplace tile? Title, short description, thumbnail, pricing model, entitlements, and deployment options?
[04:29] Marta Ruiz: Yep. Also we ask for a reference architecture diagram, a quickstart link, and a standardized security/FAQ snippet. A compliance PDF (SOC2/ISO) is helpful.

[04:40] Jordan Lee: We'll provide those. We'll also include a "reference arch" that maps Redwood components to Orion services (e.g., Redwood control plane -> Orion IAM role; runtime nodes -> Orion GPU instances). We'll attach a sample terraform/arm template if helpful.

[04:55] Priya Singh: On the perf bench 	6 quick overview: for a typical LLM chat workload (96 token prompt, 128 token response) our p99 on a ded-8 (reserved) pool is X ms 	6 note, slight mis-reads in transcription: earlier docs call out p95 vs p99 so we'll attach raw numbers. For the sync, we propose a short E2E benchmark against your dev account to validate latency and cost estimates.

[05:18] Liam O'Connor: Would you be able to quantify costs per request so we can show marketplace customers expected unit economics?
[05:24] Priya Singh: Yes 	6 we'll share an example pricing calc. For hosted managed it's per-token + per-request overhead; for Private deployment, it's a reserved capacity model with a monthly commitment and a per-token inference charge if you exceed baseline. We'll attach a sample calculator sheet.

[05:40] Marta Ruiz: On go-to-market, we also want joint marketing: a co-branded reference arch and a one-pager. Is Redwood OK with that?

[05:47] Jordan Lee: Absolutely 	6 we can do co-branded collateral. We'll coordinate on the messaging and approval flow.

[06:00] Aisha Kamal: One more security note 	6 for the managed path, do you do data residency controls by region? Some of our customers in EU require data to stay in EU regions only.

[06:09] Priya Singh: We support region pinning and routing policies. We can restrict data to EU-only clusters and provide region-specific storage. We'll document the controls and how to request GDPR-specific agreements.

[06:25] Ken Ito: On the technical side, a few deeper items we should log for SE follow-up: 1) KV cache behavior for cross-tenant prompts; 2) model pinning and rollout behaviors when a customer pins to a model version; 3) autoscaling triggers and burst behavior for Reserved pools.

[06:40] Priya Singh: I'll take those. Quick notes: KV cache is tenant-scoped; model pinning is supported via versioned model references, rollouts are canary/A-B style with automatic fallbacks. Autoscaling is policy-driven with headroom targets and is compatible with burst capacity toggles.

[06:58] Jordan Lee: Great. Let's capture items for the integration checklist: packaging for marketplace (helm/CFN), reference arch diagram, security/compliance artifacts, benchmark results, pricing calculator, co-branded collateral, and a runbook for onboarding customers.

[07:12] Marta Ruiz: For listing review cadence, after you submit the listing we'll do a sandbox test inside our staging org and ask for a functional test window. We aim for a 2-week review once we have artifacts.

[07:22] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Any blockers that would prevent us from getting the sandbox test?

[07:26] Liam O'Connor: The only potential blocker is if your helm chart assumes privileged node roles or requires kernel modules 	6 our marketplace has a hard gate on privileged operations.

[07:36] Priya Singh: We can modify the chart to avoid privileged hooks 	6 we'll validate the installer against non-privileged nodes. Good catch.

[07:46] Aisha Kamal: Also, we need documentation on key rotation and how long tokens are valid. For audits we need rotation windows and RBAC mapping for Redwood admin accounts.

[07:56] Carlos Vega: We'll provide a KMS rotation policy doc and a script for rotating service account keys.

[08:06] Jordan Lee: Any timeline constraints from your side? Marta?

[08:09] Marta Ruiz: Ideally we'd like a soft listing by mid-Jan, but realistic launch early Feb. If you can get artifacts in by Dec 23, our team will review over the holiday spike and we can queue the sandbox early Jan.

[08:22] Jordan Lee: We'll aim for that. That gives us a few action items 	6 I'll summarize after the call.

-- Mid-call clarifications / minor audio issues --
[29:05] Priya Singh: (background noise) sorry 	6 can you repeat the KMS ask?
[29:09] Aisha Kamal: We want BYOK with HSM support, exportable audit logs to S3, 12-month retention, and proof of SOC2 coverage.
[29:19] Priya Singh: Got it. We'll share the SOC2 PDF and the KMS integration doc.

[34:02] Ken Ito: Quick deep dive: autoscaler behavior 	6 how do you prevent thundering herd when a customer has spiky traffic?
[34:10] Priya Singh: We use continuous batching and queue smoothing; autoscaler uses both request rate and queue depth heuristics. There's also burst buckets which can be configured per-customer. For reserved pools, you can allocate burst credits. We'll share a tuning guide.

[39:30] Liam O'Connor: For the private endpoint option, does Redwood expect customers to open inbound ports?
[39:36] Carlos Vega: No 	6 we prefer the customer to create an outbound-only private connection to our endpoint proxy, or use a VPC endpoint so no public ingress is required. We'll include network topologies in the ref arch.

[45:05] Jordan Lee: OK I'm going to read back the next steps and owners. Jordan: share listing checklist, security artifacts (SOC2 PDF), and sample listing copy by 2026-12-23. Priya: run perf bench and share raw logs by 2026-12-29. Carlos: KMS rotation doc and installer tweak to avoid privileged hooks by 2026-12-27. Aisha/Marta: review and get sandbox dates back by 2027-01-06. Schedule follow-up Jan 7. Does that match?
[45:30] Marta Ruiz: Yes.
[45:31] Aisha Kamal: Yes.
[45:33] Ken Ito: Thx.

[45:40] Jordan Lee: Awesome. We'll also include a short demo recording (10 min) showing deploy flow and the console listing preview.
[45:47] Liam O'Connor: Please include the helm values that disable privileged operations.

[45:53] Jordan Lee: Will do. Any final Qs?
[46:00] Marta Ruiz: None from me. Happy holidays.
[46:03] Jordan Lee: Happy holidays 	6 we'll follow up via email with the artifacts and calendar invite for Jan 7.

[46:12] End of call

Notes / Links mentioned: https://redwood.example/docs/kms-integration , sample listing draft (link pending), benchmark spreadsheet (will be shared), SOC2.pdf (will be shared).

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions present (product names, acronyms), speaker labels approximate.
